methodology: These forecasts are anchored to live prediction markets and expert projections, not freehand guesses: release timing comes from Polymarket's dated release markets (GPT-5.6 ~96% by Jul 31; GPT-6 52% by Sep / 82% by Dec; Gemini 4.0 only ~10% by Jun 30; the $4.49M Claude 5 market pricing no Claude 5 before Q3) and the industry "best model" markets (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold pricing Anthropic ~64% to hold #1 at year-end, Google ~13-15% and OpenAI ~10-12% as the leading challengers). Benchmark ceilings are pinned to Epoch AI / Stanford AI Index 2026 (SWE-bench Verified effectively saturating at ~95-96% with frontier-accessible models around 88-95%) and the Artificial Analysis Index trajectory (frontier in the high-50s/low-60s on current v3/v4 scale, rising steadily but re-versioned as it saturates), then each lab's own AA/SWE back-trajectory from the historical backfill sets the slope and the gap-to-frontier. Where a market is silent on a specific lab (Zhipu, Alibaba, Meta), I extrapolate that lab's documented release cadence (~1-3 months per flagship, per the LM Council / release-pace tracker) and its current distance behind the leader, widening the uncertainty bands to reflect the thinner evidence.

marketsStory.t: Anthropic sits at ~96% on Polymarket to own the best AI model at the end of July (Google a distant 2%), a market that resolves on the Chatbot Arena leaderboard on Jul 31. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.1) the order is Fable 5 (60), GPT-5.6 Sol (59), Kimi K3 (57) and Claude Opus 4.8 (56) — and the notable move this sweep is Moonshot's Kimi K3 getting its first independent AA score at 57, edging Opus 4.8 to become the strongest open-lineage model measured, even as AA still labels it proprietary until weights ship Jul 27.

The imminent question is Google: a July Gemini reasoning flagship prices at ~78% on Polymarket, but the rumored Jul 17 GA of Gemini 3.5 Pro has not materialized — no model card, pricing or benchmarks, with Google's own blog still saying 'next month.' Further out, GPT-6 sits at ~68% by Dec 31 (only ~2% by Jul 31), a next Claude Opus at ~96% by Oct 31, and Grok 5 at ~43% before September after xAI shipped Grok 4.5 on Jul 8.

GPQA Diamond is effectively pinned near its ~94-95% noise ceiling across the frontier, so it no longer separates top models. The live coding frontier is SWE-bench Pro, where vendor-harness numbers run ~80% (Fable 5, Mythos 5) while the apples-to-apples standardized frame sits closer to ~59-64%. Kimi K3's independent 57 shows open models trailing the closed frontier by only a few points of aggregate intelligence.

Metaculus community forecasters put the median for weakly-general AI around mid-2028 and roughly a 25% chance of AGI by 2029, with strong AGI pushed toward the early 2030s. Lab CEOs cluster earlier (2026-2028) and academic skeptics later — the spread itself is the signal that capability gains remain fast but the AGI threshold stays genuinely contested.
